speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, what specific antibiotic were you taking when these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate Induced Serum Sickness-like Reaction

The rash distribution in the antecubital and popliteal fossae is highly characteristic of this condition. Given the timeline starting one week after initiating amoxicillin for sinusitis, and the combination of fever, pruritus, and arthralgia, this clinical picture strongly points to a serum sickness-like reaction. Would you like me to request blood work to check for elevated ESR or CRP levels to confirm the inflammatory nature of this reaction?
